absent: Version negotiation sequence that sets the negotiated version and flag, and use of the version lock, are not visible.
Hypervisor bounce buffer allocation and descriptor staging buffer management are not visible.
Remainder of the reclaim path after the retrieve response, including constituent unsharing and release, is truncated.
Secure monitor calling convention details and meanings of individual firmware reason codes beyond success versus error are not visible.
Initialization of the sorted memory region table and host page metadata is not visible.
Full structure layouts beyond the accessed fields of mailbox, descriptor, composite region and page records are not visible.

findings.text: Helper offers sharing of one host page with the hypervisor. It requires the host side to be in owned state and the hypervisor side to be absent, then transitions them to shared owned and shared borrowed. Failures leave the transition undone and propagate the check error.

Helper offers reversal of a single page sharing. It requires shared owned on the host side and shared borrowed on the hypervisor side plus a zero pin count, then returns them to owned and absent. Mismatched state or a busy pin count aborts without changing state.

Pin helpers manage hypervisor visibility of already shared ranges. Pinning validates shared states over the whole range, raises a per page count, and creates a hypervisor mapping on first pin. Unpinning drops the count and removes the mapping when the last pin goes away.

Range helpers expose host side only sharing for memory lending flows. They bound the frame range against the physical address width, require owned state across the range, and move it to shared owned or back to owned. The hypervisor page state is untouched.

Low level mapping helpers install or remove page table entries while a component lock is held. One creates hypervisor mappings page by page over an aligned virtual interval. Another removes hypervisor entries through a leaf and post table walk. A third installs a host stage two identity mapping with a retry after reclaiming device mappings on allocation failure.

Component locking always acquires the host stage two lock before the hypervisor page table lock and releases in reverse order. All single page share, unshare, pin and unpin operations follow this nesting, preventing opposite order acquisition in the observed paths.

A dedicated spin lock in the host mailbox state serializes mailbox setup, teardown and descriptor forwarding. Map, unmap, fragment transmit and descriptor transfer each hold it while testing presence of the transmit buffer, copying mailbox content, and updating sharing state.

Several helpers require the caller to already hold a component lock. Host range state checks and host stage two attempts assert host lock ownership, while hypervisor mapping creation asserts hypervisor page table lock ownership.

Mailbox state uses two static buffer records, one for hypervisor private bounce buffers and one for mapped host buffers, each exposing transmit and receive pointers. The host record additionally carries a lock. Separate statics track the negotiated version, a negotiated flag, and a version lock.

Mailbox mapping accepts only one exact page count derived from the mailbox page constant scaled between host and firmware page sizes, and only page aligned transmit and receive addresses. It rejects a second mapping while one is active, and reports invalid parameters or denial through a normalized result.

Mailbox teardown accepts only the host endpoint identifier and requires an active mapping. It unpins both buffers, reverses their sharing, clears the stored pointers under lock, and forwards an unmap request for the hypervisor buffers.

Host state operations first confine the interval to usable RAM. A binary search over a sorted region table locates the enclosing interval, both ends must lie in the same interval, and regions marked no map or absent regions are rejected.

State validation walks every page in the interval and demands an exact match of the expected state, failing on the first mismatch. Frame range validation separately bounds the start frame and length against the host physical address width.

A page moves from host owned with hypervisor absent to host shared owned with hypervisor shared borrowed on sharing, and back on unsharing. Unsharing is gated on zero references. Host state installation also creates a host stage two identity mapping when the page was previously absent to the host.

Descriptor transfer copies the host mailbox fragment into a hypervisor bounce buffer, shares each constituent range on the host stage two, then forwards the request. Fragmented transfers expect a fragment request response with matching length, while whole transfers expect success. Any forwarding mismatch triggers unsharing of the ranges just shared.

Host facing handlers receive a result record and a CPU context. Mapping and unmapping manage mailbox lifetime, fragment transmission handles continuation fragments, descriptor transfer handles share and lend initiations, and reclaim starts by issuing a retrieve request for the supplied handle.

Mapping unwinds in strict reverse order of acquisition, unpinning before unsharing host pages and unmapping hypervisor buffers last. Fragment handling reclaims the firmware transaction when host sharing fails, but notes that loss of earlier fragments can leave pages permanently shared without affecting confidentiality.

Unpinning performs no state validation and trusts the caller to pair each pin. Removal of the hypervisor mapping happens only on transition to zero and the code expects a full page to be unmapped at that point.

Results encode success with a success identifier and a property value, and failures with an error identifier and a numeric reason. Return propagation writes the first eight result slots into the low CPU registers and unconditionally writes the next ten as well to cover sixty four bit responses.
A call is treated as firmware framework traffic only when it is a fast call with standard owner and its function number lies within the framework range.

Pin and unpin round their virtual interval outward to page boundaries before operating. Pinning then checks shared states across the derived physical interval and installs hypervisor mappings lazily on first use of each page.

Small forwarders relay mailbox, fragment, transfer, reclaim, retrieve and release operations to the secure monitor, placing the operation identifier and its operands into designated slots and returning the monitor response to the caller. Mapping success is judged by the success identifier, otherwise the firmware reason is propagated.

Descriptor initiation validates mailbox presence, total and fragment lengths, descriptor buffer capacity, endpoint attribute placement, single endpoint with host sender and non zero composite offset, overflow free header arithmetic, and range array alignment before sharing any pages.

Constituent sharing iterates address ranges, requires page aligned address and length derived from firmware page counts, and stops at the first misaligned or failed range, reporting how many ranges succeeded so the caller can roll back exactly that prefix.
